newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut legislature convenes special session.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut legislature convenes special session.

text.p: The Connecticut legislature on Wednesday convened a special, three-day session to finish budget implementation and other bills before the start of the state's new fiscal year on July 1.
Lawmakers are expected to mop up details that could not be finished before the five-month, regular 1997 session ended on June 4.
Gov. John Rowland (R) will not participate because he is leading a trade mission to Israel.
It is not certain whether lawmakers will act on a state bonding package between $550 million and $600 million to pay for state construction projects.

Connecticut earlier this month approved a $21 billion, two-year budget that includes $394 million in new tax cuts, plus millions more in tax cuts that were previously approved but have not yet taken effect.
The state's 39-cent per gallon gasoline tax, currently the highest in the U.S., will be cut by 3 cents on July 1, and by another 3 cents on July 1, 1998.
The budget, signed by Rowland, increases overall spending by 3.7 percent over the two-year period.
